name: WISE 0855-0714
summary: The coldest known brown dwarf, 7.4 light years away, creeps west by about 8 arcseconds a year and glows only at 4 to 5 microns, so SPHEREx sees it in its longest-wavelength detectors and not in the short ones.

astrometry.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 position (J2000), proper motion and parallax via docs/research/06-targets-and-planet-x-science.md, section 1 and appendix A (SIMBAD / Gaia DR3)

grid.orientation: north up, east left: row 0 is the north (top) row, column 0 the east (left) column; pixel (x, y) = (column, row), 0-based pixel centres; FITS equivalent CRPIX1 = CRPIX2 = 61, CDELT1 = CDELT2 = -3/3600 deg (row index increases southward)
grid.fileFormat: raw little-endian float32, row-major, 121 x 121 values, MJy/sr after background subtraction, NaN = no data

groups.label: 3.8 to 5.0 micron (detectors D5 and D6 stacked)

display.formula: t = clip((v - vmin) / (vmax - vmin), 0, 1); out = asinh(t / soft) / asinh(1 / soft)

displayExposure.formula: t = clip((v - vmin) / (vmax - vmin), 0, 1); out = asinh(t / soft) / asinh(1 / soft)

groups.stackMethod: Inverse-variance weighted mean of the reprojected exposures; weight 1/sigma_i^2 with sigma_i = 1.4826 x MAD of the finite pixels of exposure i on the grid. Passes with 5 or more exposures: each grid pixel with at least 5 finite values is sigma-clipped across exposures first (reject |value - median| > 4 x 1.4826 x MAD of that pixel's values, up to 3 iterations). Per-pixel scatter is used as the clipping sigma, not the background sigma_i, so that stars, whose flux changes with the wavelength sampled, are not clipped. NaN where no exposure has data.

truth.note: motionArcsec is measured: difference of the stack centroids of the first and last passes with a detection (S/N >= 5); predictedMotionArcsec comes from the astrometry (proper motion + parallax).

challengeInput.note: The challenge's coordinates (08h55m10.831s, -07d14m42.53s) are the WISE-era position (epoch about 2010.45, notes 06 and 08). Both they and the 2025 to 2026 position fall inside this field.

caveats: In the D2 group a normal star (CatWISE2020 J085501.95-071428.2) 4 to 8 arcsec from WISE 0855 is clearly visible next to the predicted position (pass field blendedWith); WISE 0855 itself does not show at 1.1 to 1.65 micron.
At 0.6 to 1.3 SPHEREx pixels per pass the motion is subtle: zoom in and use the markers.
A static star (CatWISE2020 J085501.95-071428.2, W1 15.0) lies 4 to 11 arcsec from WISE 0855 during the SPHEREx baseline and blends with it in D5 and in the short-wavelength detectors (note 08).
The challenge coordinates are the WISE-era (about 2010.45) position, 2 arcmin east of where the brown dwarf is in 2025 and 2026.

choicesAfterLooking: Attribution rule: a centroid closer to the known static star CatWISE2020 J085501.95-071428.2 than to the prediction is credited to that star (pass field blendedWith) and the target counts as not detected. Added after the pre-set S/N >= 5 rule 'detected' WISE 0855 in 3 of 4 D2 passes: those centroids sit 0.06 to 0.43 arcsec from the star.
provenance.zodi: not subtracted (a sigma-clipped median of the box is enough for fields of a few arcmin, note 09)
provenance.flags: not read and not applied (the FLAGS mask erases saturated stars, note 08)
